Servitude for six years is for Hebrew servants (21:2); it is not the penalty for a negligent ox owner.
In Exodus 22, if an Israelite stole an ox and then slaughtered or sold it, what restitution was required?
A thief who stole an ox and slaughtered or sold it “must repay five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep” (22:1).
Exodus 22:1
One ox
One ox is the animal itself, not the penalty; the law demanded five oxen for a stolen ox that was slaughtered or sold (22:1).
Two oxen
Double was the penalty if the stolen animal was found alive in the thief’s possession (22:4), not if it was slaughtered or sold.
Four oxen
Four was the penalty for a sheep, not for an ox (22:1).
Five oxen
Seven oxen
Seven oxen is not the penalty in this law; the text says five oxen for an ox (22:1).
In the case laws of Exodus 22, if a stolen donkey, ox, or sheep was found alive in the thief’s possession, what did the thief have to pay?
If the stolen animal was found alive in his possession, “he must pay back double” (22:4).
Exodus 22:4
Nothing if it was returned
Returning the animal was not enough; the thief also had to pay back double (22:4).
Half its value
Half its value is not the penalty; the law says double (22:4).
Double
Four times its value
Four times is the penalty for a slaughtered or sold sheep, not for one found alive (22:1, 22:4).
Five times its value
Five times is the penalty for a slaughtered or sold ox (22:1); an animal found alive required double (22:4).
According to Exodus 22, when was there bloodguilt for killing a thief who broke into a house?
A thief beaten to death while breaking in brought no bloodguilt (22:2), but “if it happens after sunrise, there is guilt for his bloodshed” (22:3).
Exodus 22:2-3
Never
Bloodguilt did not apply in every case; at night there was none (22:2), but after sunrise there was guilt (22:3).
Only if the thief was armed
Being armed is not mentioned; the difference in the law is whether it was after sunrise (22:3).
If it happened after sunrise
Only in Egypt
The law was given to Israel at Sinai; it does not limit bloodguilt to Egypt (22:3).
Only on the Sabbath
The Sabbath is not mentioned in this law; the rule turns on sunrise (22:3).
In Exodus 22, if a man let his animals graze in another person’s field or vineyard, how was he to make restitution?
A man whose livestock grazed in another’s field “must make restitution from the best of his own field or vineyard” (22:5).
Exodus 22:5
From the poorest part of his land
The law required restitution from the best of his own field or vineyard, not the poorest part (22:5).
From the best of his own field and vineyard
With silver only
The law names restitution from the best of his own field or vineyard, not silver only (22:5).
By fasting for seven days
Fasting is not part of this law; the restitution was from the best of his own field or vineyard (22:5).
By giving one animal
Giving one animal is not mentioned; restitution came from the best of his own field or vineyard (22:5).
In the Sinai laws of Exodus 22, if a fire spread and consumed stacked grain, standing grain, or a field, what was required of the one who started the fire?
“The one who started the fire must make full restitution” (22:6).
Exodus 22:6
A sin offering only
A sin offering is not mentioned in this law, which demands full restitution (22:6).
One day of labor
Labor is not the penalty; the law demands full restitution (22:6).
Full restitution
Double restitution only if witnesses saw it
The law does not depend on witnesses; whoever started the fire must make full restitution (22:6).
No payment if it was accidental
The law does not excuse accidents; the one who started the fire must make full restitution (22:6).
In Exodus 22, what were Israelites forbidden to charge when lending money to a poor fellow Israelite?
“You are not to charge him interest” when lending to a poor person among God’s people (22:25).
Exodus 22:25
Interest
Tax
Tax is not what the law forbids here; it forbids charging a poor person interest (22:25).
Tithe
Tithes were given to God, not charged on a loan; the law forbids interest on loans to the poor (22:25).
Rent
Rent is not the subject of this command; it forbids charging interest to the poor (22:25).
Wages
Wages are not the subject of this command; it forbids charging interest (22:25).
In Exodus 22, why were the people of Israel told not to mistreat or oppress a foreigner?
“You must not exploit or oppress a foreign resident, for you yourselves were foreigners in the land of Egypt” (22:21).
Exodus 22:21
Foreigners paid the temple tax
No temple tax is mentioned in this law; the reason given is Israel’s own time as foreigners in Egypt (22:21).
Moses had married a foreigner
Moses’ marriage is not the reason; the reason given is that Israel had been foreigners in Egypt (22:21).
They had been foreigners in Egypt
Foreigners owned the land first
The law does not say foreigners owned the land first; the reason is that Israel had been foreigners in Egypt (22:21).
Pharaoh had commanded it
Pharaoh did not command this; God gave the law and appealed to Israel’s time in Egypt (22:21).
According to Exodus 22, by when did a lender have to return a poor man’s cloak if it had been taken as a pledge?
“If you take your neighbor’s cloak as collateral, return it to him by sunset” (22:26).
Exodus 22:26-27
By sunrise
The cloak was to be returned by sunset, not sunrise, since he needed it to sleep in (22:26–27).
By sunset
By the next Sabbath
The Sabbath is not mentioned; the cloak was to be returned by sunset (22:26).
By the new moon
The new moon is not mentioned; the cloak was to be returned by sunset (22:26).
At the end of the year
The end of the year is far too late; the cloak was to be returned by sunset (22:26).
In Exodus 22, what was the command concerning a sorceress?
“You must not allow a sorceress to live” (22:18).
Exodus 22:18
Exile her
Exile is not the penalty given; the law says not to allow her to live (22:18).
Fine her
A fine is not the penalty given; the law says not to allow her to live (22:18).
Put her in prison
Prison is not the penalty given; the law says not to allow her to live (22:18).
Do not allow her to live
Make her serve at the sanctuary
Serving at the sanctuary is not mentioned; the law says not to allow her to live (22:18).
In the laws of Exodus 22, what penalty was given for a person who lay with an animal?
“Whoever lies with an animal must surely be put to death” (22:19).
Exodus 22:19
Double restitution
Double restitution applied to theft (22:4, 22:9), not to this offense; the penalty here is death (22:19).
Exile from the camp
Exile is not the penalty given; the law says the person must surely be put to death (22:19).
Put to death
Forty lashes
Forty lashes are not mentioned in this law; the penalty is death (22:19).
Public confession only
A public confession alone is not mentioned; the law says the person must surely be put to death (22:19).
According to Exodus 22, what was to happen to anyone who sacrificed to any god other than the LORD alone?
Anyone who sacrifices “to any god other than the LORD alone” must “be set apart for destruction” (22:20).
Exodus 22:20
He would pay a ram
Paying a ram is not the penalty given; the law says he must be set apart for destruction (22:20).
He would be set apart for destruction
He would wash and be clean
Washing to be clean is not the penalty given; he must be set apart for destruction (22:20).
He would move outside the camp for a month
Moving outside the camp for a month is not mentioned; the penalty is destruction (22:20).
He would bring firstfruits
Bringing firstfruits is not the remedy; the penalty is destruction (22:20).
In Exodus 22, if anyone mistreated widows or fatherless children and they cried out to the LORD, what did He warn He would do to the oppressors?
If they mistreat widows or orphans and these cry out, the LORD says, “I will kill you with the sword; then your wives will become widows and your children will be fatherless” (22:22–24).
Exodus 22:22-24
Send rain
God did not promise rain; He warned that He would kill the oppressors with the sword (22:24).
Ignore them
The LORD says the opposite: “I will surely hear their cry” (22:23).
Judge only the leaders
God did not limit this to leaders; He addressed anyone who mistreated widows or orphans (22:22–24).
Kill them with the sword
Send them to another tribe
Sending them to another tribe is not mentioned; the LORD warned that He would kill the oppressors with the sword (22:24).
In Exodus 22, besides not blaspheming God, whom were the Israelites forbidden to curse?
“You must not blaspheme God or curse the ruler of your people” (22:28).
Exodus 22:28
A priest from Levi
The verse names the ruler of the people, not a priest from Levi (22:28).
The ruler of their people
A judge from another tribe
The verse names the ruler of the people, not a judge from another tribe (22:28).
Their parents only
Cursing a father or mother was also forbidden (Exodus 21:17), but the person named alongside God in this verse is the ruler of the people (22:28).
A visiting prophet
A visiting prophet is not named; the verse forbids cursing the ruler of your people (22:28).
In the closing commands of Exodus 22, how long was a firstborn ox or sheep to remain with its mother before being given to the LORD?
The young animals were to “stay with their mothers for seven days, but on the eighth day you are to give them to Me” (22:30).
Exodus 22:30
Three days
Three days is not the time given; the young stayed seven days (22:30).
Seven days
Fourteen days
Fourteen days is twice the time given; the young stayed seven days (22:30).
Thirty days
Thirty days is not the time given; the young stayed seven days (22:30).
One year
One year is not the time given; the young stayed seven days and were given on the eighth day (22:30).
In Exodus 22, what were God’s holy people to do with meat from an animal torn by wild beasts in the field?
“You must not eat the meat of a mauled animal found in the field; you are to throw it to the dogs” (22:31).
Exodus 22:31
Eat it after washing it
Washing does not make torn meat acceptable; it was to be thrown to the dogs (22:31).
Burn it on the altar
It was not to be burned on the altar; it was to be thrown to the dogs (22:31).
Sell it to foreigners
Selling it to foreigners is not mentioned; it was to be thrown to the dogs (22:31).
Bury it outside the camp
Burying it is not what the law says; it was to be thrown to the dogs (22:31).
Throw it to the dogs

Nothing
Paying nothing is not allowed; the man still had to pay (22:17).
A trespass offering only
A trespass offering is not mentioned; the man still had to pay an amount comparable to the bridal price (22:17).
Double the bride-price
Double the bride-price is not stated; the amount was comparable to the bridal price of a virgin (22:17).
The customary bride-price for virgins
A field in her name
A field in her name is not mentioned; he paid an amount comparable to the bridal price (22:17).
In the property laws of Exodus 22, if money or goods were left with a neighbor for safekeeping, but the thief was not found, what happened next?

Exodus 22:7-8
The loss was automatically shared
The loss was not automatically shared; the keeper appeared before the judges (22:8).
The owner of the house appeared before the judges
The priest decided by lot
A priest casting lots is not mentioned here; the keeper appeared before the judges (22:8).
The lender paid double
No lender is involved; the owner of the house appeared before the judges (22:8).
The matter was dropped
The matter was not dropped; the keeper appeared before the judges (22:8).
According to Exodus 22, in a dispute over ownership of an ox, donkey, sheep, garment, or other lost item, what did the person condemned by the judges have to do?
“The one whom the judges find guilty must pay back double to his neighbor” (22:9).
Exodus 22:9
Offer a burnt offering
A burnt offering is not the penalty here; the guilty party paid back double (22:9).
Leave the city
Leaving the city is not mentioned; the guilty party paid back double (22:9).
Pay double to his neighbor
Pay back only the item itself
Repaying only the item would be less than the law demands; the guilty party paid back double (22:9).
Serve six years
Serving six years is not mentioned in this law; the guilty party paid back double (22:9).
In Exodus 22, if someone was given another man’s animal to care for and it died, was injured, or was stolen while no one was watching, what settled whether the keeper had taken it?

Exodus 22:10-11
A written contract
No written contract is mentioned; the matter was settled by an oath before the LORD (22:11).
The testimony of one relative
A relative’s testimony is not mentioned; the matter was settled by an oath before the LORD (22:11).
An oath before the LORD
Payment of half its value
Half its value is not the remedy; an oath before the LORD settled the matter, and the owner accepted it (22:11).
Casting lots outside the camp
Casting lots is not mentioned in this law; the matter was settled by an oath before the LORD (22:11).

The owner was absent and the animal was borrowed
If the owner was absent and the animal was borrowed, the borrower had to make full restitution (22:14).
The animal had been hired, or the owner was present
The borrower was poor
Poverty is not mentioned in this law; a borrower owed full restitution when the owner was absent (22:14).
The injury happened at night
Nighttime is not mentioned in this law; full restitution depended on the owner’s absence (22:14).
The animal was from a foreigner
The owner being a foreigner is not mentioned in this law; full restitution depended on the owner’s absence (22:14).
In the Sabbath instruction in Exodus 23, on which day were Israelites, their oxen, their donkeys, and the foreign resident to rest and be refreshed?

Exodus 23:12
The first day

The third day

The seventh day
The eighth day
The eighth day is when a boy is circumcised (Leviticus 12:3) and the last day of Tabernacles (Leviticus 23:36), not the weekly rest.
The fiftieth day

One time

Two times

Three times

Seven times

In Exodus 23, which feast was to be kept in the month of Abib because that was the month Israel came out of Egypt?

Exodus 23:15
The Feast of Harvest
The Feast of Harvest comes with the firstfruits of what is sown in the field (23:16), later in the year.
The Feast of Ingathering
The Feast of Ingathering is kept at the end of the year when the produce is gathered (23:16).
The Feast of Unleavened Bread
The Feast of Trumpets

Keep it until the owner paid a fee

At Mount Sinai in Exodus 24, after Moses told the people all the LORD’s words and laws, how did all the people answer?

Joshua

A monthly new moon is not part of this command; the Ingathering is at the turn of the year (34:22).

The exile is centuries later; this feast is commanded at Sinai for the turn of the year (34:22).
In Exodus 34, how often were all the males of Israel to appear before the Lord GOD, the God of Israel?
“Three times a year all your males are to appear before the Lord GOD, the God of Israel” (34:23).
Exodus 34:23
Once a month
Once a month is not what the text says; the males appear three times a year (34:23).
Twice a year
Twice a year is not what the text says; 34:23 gives three times.
Three times a year

The weekly Sabbath is a rest (34:21), not the pilgrimage appearance of 34:23.

A seven-year interval is not mentioned; 34:23 and 34:24 say three times a year.
In the offering instructions of Exodus 34, what was Israel told to bring to the house of the LORD?
“Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God” (34:26).
Exodus 34:26
Only the oldest animals from the herds
Old animals are not mentioned; the command concerns the best of the firstfruits of the soil (34:26).

Cedar logs cut in the forests of Lebanon
Cedar from Lebanon was Solomon’s building material for the temple (1 Kings 5:6), not part of this offering command.
Incense bought from the traders of Sheba
Sheba’s spices were brought to Solomon (1 Kings 10:2); this command concerns firstfruits of the soil (34:26).

Repaint them and dedicate them to the LORD

Leaving them untouched is the opposite of the command (34:13).
Tear them down, smash them, and cut them down

Moving them outside the camp is not commanded; they were to be destroyed (34:13).
In Exodus 34, what reason is given for not worshiping another god?

Because Israel was weak in battle
Weakness in battle is not the reason given; the reason is the LORD’s jealous name (34:14).

Because the LORD’s name is Jealous

Music is not mentioned in this command; the reason is His jealous name (34:14).

Angels are not mentioned as punishers; the reason is that the LORD is a jealous God (34:14).
In Exodus 34:12, if Israel made a treaty with the inhabitants of the land, what might those inhabitants become in Israel’s midst?

A harvest blessing
A harvest blessing is the opposite of the warning; the danger was a snare (34:12).
A royal alliance

A snare
A memorial
A memorial is not mentioned; the danger was a snare (34:12).

Showbread

No tithe meal is mentioned; the warning was about eating their sacrifices (34:15).
Meat from his sacrifice
Locusts and wild honey

In Exodus 34, what was not to be offered along with the blood of the LORD’s sacrifices?
The LORD said, “Do not offer the blood of a sacrifice to Me along with anything leavened” (34:25).
Exodus 34:25
Oil
Oil belongs on grain offerings (Leviticus 2:1); it is not the thing forbidden in 34:25.
Salt
Salt was required on offerings (Leviticus 2:13), not forbidden.
Incense
Fragrant incense was burned by Aaron (Exodus 30:7); it is not what 34:25 forbids.
Wine
Wine was the drink offering with burnt offerings and sacrifices (Numbers 15:5), not what 34:25 forbids.
Anything leavened

Exodus 34:25
The incense on the altar

The sacrifice of the Passover Feast
The manna in the jar

The lamp oil in the tabernacle

The priest’s robe
A priest’s robe is not mentioned; 34:25 concerns the Passover sacrifice.
In Exodus 34, what food preparation was specifically forbidden in these covenant commands?
“You must not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk” (34:26).

Boiling manna with oil

Roasting grain on the Sabbath

Cooking a young goat in its mother’s milk
Baking bread without salt
Salt was required on offerings (Leviticus 2:13); baking without it is not forbidden in 34:26.
Eating fish during a fast
Fasting and eating fish are not mentioned in these commands; the food rule is about a young goat (34:26).
In the firstborn instructions of Exodus 34, which male animals were specifically said to belong to the LORD?
“The first offspring of every womb belongs to Me, including all the firstborn males among your livestock, whether cattle or sheep” (34:19).

Every tenth animal only

Every unclean animal

Only firstborn rams
The text says firstborn males of cattle or sheep, not only rams (34:19).
Only animals brought from Egypt
The law is not limited to animals from Egypt; it covers all firstborn males of livestock (34:19).
In Moses’ prayer in Exodus 34, after calling Israel a stiff-necked people and asking for pardon, what did he ask the LORD to make Israel?

A kingdom like Egypt

His inheritance

Rulers over Edom
Rule over Edom is not part of Moses’ prayer (34:9).
A nation without borders
Borders are not part of the prayer; Moses asked to be taken as God’s inheritance (34:9).
In the LORD’s proclamation to Moses in Exodus 34, for how many generations does He maintain loving devotion?
The LORD proclaimed “maintaining loving devotion to a thousand generations” (34:7).
Exodus 34:7
Seven generations
Seven generations is not the number; the iniquity of the fathers is visited to the third and fourth generations (34:7), while loving devotion lasts a thousand.
Seventy generations

One hundred generations
One hundred generations is not the number given in 34:7; it is a thousand.
A thousand generations
Forever without any number given
A number is given in 34:7: a thousand generations.
In the renewed covenant of Exodus 34, what did the LORD promise to do before all Israel that had not been done in all the earth or in any nation?
“Before all your people I will perform wonders that have never been done in any nation in all the world” (34:10).
Exodus 34:10
Send daily manna forever

Build the temple immediately

Perform wonders
Appoint kings over every tribe
Kings were appointed later, in the days of Samuel (1 Samuel 8:22); this promise is about wonders (34:10).
Silence all foreign languages
Language was confused at Babel (Genesis 11:7), not silenced as a wonder here.
In Exodus 34, which people group is not included in the list of nations the LORD said He would drive out before Israel?

Amorites
The Amorites are the first people named in 34:11.
Hivites

Jebusites
The Jebusites are the last people named in 34:11.
Girgashites
Perizzites

When all Israelite males were commanded in Exodus 34 to appear before the LORD three times a year, what special promise did God make about their land?

Only Joshua, who waited at the foot of the mountain

When he blessed the people at the altar

When he entered before the LORD to speak with Him

Aaron and incense are not part of this passage; the veil was removed before the LORD (34:34).

Sleeping outside the camp is not mentioned; the veil came off when he spoke with the LORD (34:34).

The tribal censuses of Israel

The songs of deliverance

The plans for the tabernacle furniture begin in Exodus 25, not on the tablets (34:28).
The names of the patriarchs
The names of the patriarchs are not mentioned as written on the tablets; the covenant words were (34:28).
In the LORD’s self-proclamation to Moses in Exodus 34:6, which qualities come immediately after “compassionate and gracious”?

Six days
Seven days

Baking bread

Gathering manna

Lighting a fire
Drawing water
Drawing water is not named; the Sabbath ban here concerns lighting fires in dwellings (35:3).
Pitching tents
Pitching tents is not named; the ban here concerns lighting fires in dwellings (35:3).

When Moses listed materials for the sanctuary in Exodus 35, which precious metal was named first?

Silver

Gold
Lead
Lead is not among the materials Moses lists for the sanctuary (35:5–9).

Camel hair

Goat hair

After Moses finished giving the instructions in Exodus 35, what did the whole congregation of Israel do next?

Crossed the Jordan

In Exodus 35, which tribe did Bezalel, the craftsman called by name, belong to?

Judah
Ephraim

Dan

In the tabernacle inventory of Exodus 35, which item is mentioned together with its poles, utensils, and the Bread of the Presence?

The ark

The lampstand

The table
The basin

In Exodus 35, which sacred object is listed with its poles, the mercy seat, and the veil?

The ark

The lampstand

Tunics for all firstborn males

Which combined description accurately summarizes the craftsmen in Exodus 35?

Moses names “Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah” (35:30) and “Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan” (35:34), filled “with skill to do all kinds of work as engravers, designers, embroiderers” (35:35).
Bezalel of Levi and Oholiab of Benjamin were chosen only to guard the tabernacle gate and carry its furnishings on the march
Bezalel was of Judah and Oholiab of Dan, and they were craftsmen, not gate guards (35:30–35).
Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of Judah, and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of Dan, were filled with skill for designing, engraving, embroidering, and weaving
Aaron and Joshua were appointed by Moses to cut stones and carve wood, and to teach the elders how to build the ark
Aaron was the priest and Joshua was Moses’ assistant; the chapter names Bezalel and Oholiab as craftsmen (35:30–35).
Hur and Caleb, both of Judah, were filled with skill only for metalwork and were forbidden to teach anyone else
Hur was Bezalel’s grandfather (35:30), and the skill given was broader than metalwork (35:31–35).
