The lampstands
The lampstands are golden (1:12), not bronze.
His feet
His hands
His right hand holds seven stars (1:16); the bronze image is for His feet.
The gates
No gates appear in Revelation 1; the polished bronze describes His feet.
In Revelation 1:15, what was like the roar of many waters?
“His voice was like the roar of many waters” (1:15).
Revelation 1:15
His face
His face was like the sun shining at its brightest (1:16).
His robe
His robe is described as long (1:13), not compared to water.
The trumpet
The voice John first heard was like a trumpet (1:10); the many-waters image belongs to His voice in 1:15.
His voice
The island sea
John was on an island (1:9), but the roar of many waters describes His voice.
What did the glorious figure hold in His right hand in Revelation 1:16?
“He held in His right hand seven stars” (1:16).
Revelation 1:16
Seven seals
The seven seals are on the scroll in Revelation 5:1, not in His hand in 1:16.
Seven stars
A golden censer
An angel holds a golden censer in Revelation 8:3; Christ holds seven stars.
A shepherd’s staff
No staff is mentioned in Revelation 1; He held seven stars in His right hand.
A stone tablet
Moses carried stone tablets (Exodus 34:1); Christ holds seven stars in 1:16.
In Revelation 1:16, what came out of His mouth?
“A sharp double-edged sword came from His mouth” (1:16).
Revelation 1:16
A sharp double-edged sword
A stream of fire
Fire comes from the mouths of the horses in Revelation 9:17; from Christ’s mouth comes a sword.
A trumpet blast
His voice was like a trumpet (1:10), but what came from His mouth was a sword.
A rod of iron
He will rule the nations “with an iron scepter” (Revelation 19:15), but a sword proceeds from His mouth.
Seven flashes of lightning
Flashes of lightning come from the throne in Revelation 4:5, not from His mouth in 1:16.
In Revelation 1:16, what was His face like?
“His face was like the sun shining at its brightest” (1:16).
Revelation 1:16
The moon at full brightness
The moon is not mentioned in Revelation 1; His face is like the sun.
Lightning in a storm
The angel in Daniel 10:6 had “his face like the brilliance of lightning”; Christ’s face is like the sun.
A polished gem
No gem imagery is used for His face; it was like the sun shining at its brightest.
A burning altar
No altar appears in Revelation 1; His face was like the sun.
The sun shining at its brightest
How did John react when he saw the glorious figure in Revelation 1:17?
“When I saw Him, I fell at His feet like a dead man” (1:17).
Revelation 1:17
He shouted for joy
John did not shout for joy; he fell at His feet like a dead man.
He ran to the shore
John did not run anywhere; he fell at His feet like a dead man (1:17).
He fell at His feet like a dead man
He hid behind the lampstands
John did not hide; he fell at His feet like a dead man.
He asked for a scroll
John had already been told to write on a scroll (1:11); when he saw Christ he fell down.
After John fell in Revelation 1:17, how was he reassured?
“He placed His right hand on me and said, ‘Do not be afraid’” (1:17).
Revelation 1:17
An angel lifted him up with his wings and set him on his feet
No angel lifts John; Christ Himself placed His right hand on him (1:17).
A trumpet sounded again and a voice told him to stand up

Angels, elders, and living creatures are not the group named in 18:20.
Heaven, saints, apostles, and prophets
Israel, Judah, Levi, and Benjamin
Israel, Judah, Levi, and Benjamin are not named in Revelation 18.
Kings, captains, mighty men, and slaves
Kings, captains, mighty men, and slaves are mentioned in other passages, not in the call to rejoice.
Pastors, teachers, evangelists, and deacons
Pastors, teachers, evangelists, and deacons are not named in Revelation 18.
In the opening praise scene of Revelation 19, what word does the great multitude in heaven shout?
The great multitude in heaven begins with “Hallelujah!” in 19:1, celebrating salvation and God’s judgments.
Revelation 19:1
Hosanna
Hosanna was the crowd’s cry when Jesus entered Jerusalem (Matthew 21:9), not the word this heavenly multitude shouts.
Hallelujah
Selah
Selah is a pause marker in the Psalms (for example Psalm 3:2), not a word shouted in Revelation 19.
Maranatha
Maranatha is an Aramaic prayer found in Paul’s letters, not a word the multitude cries out in this chapter.
Amen
“Amen” is added only by the elders and living creatures in 19:4, after the multitude has already cried “Hallelujah!”
In Revelation 19, which three things are said to belong to God?
The multitude shouts, “Hallelujah! Salvation and glory and power belong to our God!” (19:1).
Revelation 19:1
Wisdom, riches, and strength
Power, riches, wisdom and strength appear in the Lamb’s praise in Revelation 5:12, but not as the three things named in 19:1.
Grace, peace, and mercy
Grace, peace and mercy are greetings and blessings in the letters, not the three things the multitude says belong to God.
Salvation, glory, and power
Faith, hope, and love
Faith, hope and love are Paul’s trio in 1 Corinthians 13, not the things ascribed to God in this heavenly shout.
Kingdom, priesthood, and prophecy
Kingdom, priesthood and prophecy are not the three things in the multitude’s cry; 19:1 names salvation, glory and power.
In the heavenly hallelujah of Revelation 19, how are God’s judgments described?
The multitude praises God because “His judgments are true and just” (19:2).
Revelation 19:2
Deep and mysterious
God’s judgments are not called deep or mysterious here; the praise says they are “true and just.”
Swift and hidden
Nothing in the praise calls God’s judgments swift or hidden; they are declared “true and just” openly in heaven.
True and just
Terrible and secret
Nothing in the praise calls God’s judgments terrible or secret; the multitude says they are “true and just.”
Ancient and unsearchable
Unsearchable judgments are a theme of Romans 11:33, but here the multitude calls them “true and just.”
In Revelation 19, whom has God judged for corrupting the earth?
God “has judged the great prostitute who corrupted the earth with her immorality” (19:2).
Revelation 19:2
The dragon
The dragon is dealt with elsewhere in Revelation (20:2–3), but 19:2 names the great prostitute as the one judged for corrupting the earth.
Jezebel
Jezebel is the woman rebuked in the letter to Thyatira (Revelation 2:20), not the one judged for corrupting the earth in 19:2.
The false prophet
The false prophet is captured later in the chapter (19:20); the judgment in 19:2 is on the great prostitute.
The great prostitute
Gog
Gog belongs to Ezekiel’s prophecy and is not named in Revelation 19, where the one judged for corrupting the earth is the great prostitute.
In John’s vision in Revelation 19, what did the great prostitute do to the earth?
She “corrupted the earth with her immorality” (19:2).
Revelation 19:2
She scorched it with fire
No fire is said to be what she did; 19:2 says she corrupted the earth with her immorality (her smoke rises in 19:3 as her judgment).
She filled it with idols only
Idolatry is not what 19:2 charges her with; it says she corrupted the earth with her immorality.
She corrupted it with her immorality
She drowned it with floods
Floods are not mentioned in her charge; she corrupted the earth with her immorality (19:2).
She covered it with darkness
Darkness is not what she is charged with; 19:2 says she corrupted the earth with her immorality.
In Revelation 19, whose blood has God avenged?
God “has avenged the blood of His servants that was poured out by her hand” (19:2).
Revelation 19:2
The prophets of Baal
The prophets of Baal were put to death at the Kishon Valley (1 Kings 18:40); 19:2 speaks of the blood of God’s servants.
His servants
The kings of Judah
The kings of Judah are not the ones whose blood is avenged in 19:2; it is the blood of His servants.
The angels of heaven
Angels are not killed by her hand; the blood avenged in 19:2 is that of God’s servants.
The tribes of Ephraim
The tribes of Ephraim are not mentioned in Revelation 19; the blood avenged is that of His servants (19:2).
In the second hallelujah of Revelation 19, what is said to rise forever and ever?
The second hallelujah says, “Her smoke rises forever and ever” (19:3).
Revelation 19:3
Incense
Incense rises before God’s throne with the saints’ prayers (Revelation 8:3), but 19:3 says her smoke rises forever.
Fire from the altar
Fire from the altar is hurled to the earth in Revelation 8:5; the rising thing in 19:3 is her smoke.
Her smoke
The morning star
The morning star is a title of Jesus (Revelation 22:16), not something that rises in the second hallelujah.
A trumpet sound
Trumpet sounds belong to the seven trumpets (Revelation 8–11); in 19:3 it is her smoke that rises.
In Revelation 19, which beings fall down and say, “Amen, Hallelujah!”?
“The twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshiped God who sits on the throne, saying: ‘Amen, Hallelujah!’” (19:4).
Revelation 19:4
The seven angels with trumpets
The seven angels with trumpets sound their trumpets in Revelation 8–11; they are not the ones who say “Amen, Hallelujah!” in 19:4.
The martyrs under the altar
The martyrs under the altar cry out for justice in Revelation 6:9–10; they do not say “Amen, Hallelujah!” here.
The twenty-four elders and the four living creatures
The twelve apostles and the tribes
The twelve apostles and the tribes are not named in 19:4; the worshipers are the elders and living creatures.
The saints on Mount Zion
The 144,000 stand with the Lamb on Mount Zion in Revelation 14:1; the ones who fall down in 19:4 are the elders and living creatures.
In Revelation 19, who is described as sitting on the throne?
The elders and living creatures worship “God who sits on the throne” (19:4).
Revelation 19:4
Michael
Michael fights the dragon in Revelation 12:7; 19:4 says it is God who sits on the throne.
The Lamb only
The Lamb is worshiped with God elsewhere, but 19:4 states plainly that God is the one who sits on the throne.
God
One of the elders
The elders sit on thrones around the throne (Revelation 4:4); 19:4 says God sits on the throne itself.
The Ancient Serpent
The Ancient Serpent is the devil, bound for a thousand years (Revelation 20:2), and is not on the throne.
In Revelation 19, from where does the voice come that says, “Praise our God”?
“Then a voice came from the throne, saying: ‘Praise our God…’” (19:5).
Revelation 19:5
From the sea
The sea is not the source of this voice; 19:5 says it came from the throne.
From the temple
No voice from the temple is mentioned in 19:5; the voice came from the throne.
From the wilderness
The wilderness is where the woman is nourished (Revelation 12:6), not the source of the voice in 19:5.
From the throne
From the altar
The altar holds the martyrs’ souls (Revelation 6:9), but the voice that says “Praise our God” came from the throne.
In Revelation 19, who are called to praise God?
The voice from the throne calls, “Praise our God, all you who serve Him, and those who fear Him, small and great alike!” (19:5).
Revelation 19:5
Only the prophets
The call is not limited to prophets; it goes to all who serve and fear God, small and great alike (19:5).
Only Israel
The call is not limited to Israel; it goes to all who serve and fear God, small and great alike (19:5).
All who serve Him and fear Him
Only the martyrs
The call is not limited to martyrs; it goes to all who serve and fear God, small and great alike (19:5).
Only the angels
The call is not limited to angels; it goes to all who serve and fear God, small and great alike (19:5).
In the great heavenly cry of Revelation 19, who reigns?
The multitude cries, “Hallelujah! For the Lord our God the Almighty reigns” (19:6).
Revelation 19:6
The Lamb’s bride
The bride has made herself ready (19:7); the reigning one in 19:6 is the Lord our God the Almighty.
The Lord our God the Almighty
The archangel Michael
Michael fights the dragon in Revelation 12:7 but is not the one said to reign in 19:6.
The elders of heaven
The elders worship God (19:4); it is the Lord our God the Almighty who reigns in 19:6.
The nations redeemed
Redeemed nations are not the ones who reign in 19:6; the cry says the Lord our God the Almighty reigns.
In Revelation 19, what has come that causes rejoicing?
The multitude says, “the marriage of the Lamb has come” (19:7), and calls for rejoicing.
Revelation 19:7
The thousand years
The thousand years are described in Revelation 20, after this chapter, not announced in 19:7.
The new Jerusalem
The new Jerusalem comes down in Revelation 21:2, after this scene; in 19:7 the marriage of the Lamb has come.
The marriage of the Lamb
The seventh trumpet
The seventh trumpet sounds in Revelation 11:15; in 19:7 the cause for rejoicing is the marriage of the Lamb.
The first resurrection
The first resurrection is described in Revelation 20:5–6; the rejoicing in 19:7 is for the marriage of the Lamb.
In Revelation 19, who has made herself ready?
“His bride has made herself ready” (19:7).
Revelation 19:7
The church in Laodicea
Laodicea is one of the seven churches addressed in Revelation 3:14–22; 19:7 says the bride has made herself ready.
The holy city
The holy city is described as a bride in Revelation 21:2, but in 19:7 it is “His bride” who has made herself ready.
The bride
The woman in the wilderness
The woman in the wilderness is a figure from Revelation 12:6, not the one who prepares herself in 19:7.
The daughter of Zion
The daughter of Zion is an Old Testament image and is not named in Revelation 19; the one made ready is the bride.
In Revelation 19, what clothing is given to the bride?
“She was given clothing of fine linen, bright and pure” (19:8).
Revelation 19:8
Purple and scarlet
Purple and scarlet clothe the woman called the great prostitute (Revelation 17:4), not the bride in 19:8.
Sackcloth and ashes
Sackcloth and ashes are signs of mourning, but the bride is given fine linen, bright and pure (19:8).
Fine linen, bright and pure
White wool and gold
White wool describes the hair of the Son of Man (Revelation 1:14); the bride’s clothing in 19:8 is fine linen.
Linen mixed with blue and red
Linen mixed with blue and red is not what the bride is given; 19:8 says it is fine linen, bright and pure.
In Revelation 19, what does the bride’s fine linen represent?
“The fine linen she wears is the righteous acts of the saints” (19:8).
Revelation 19:8
The law of Moses
The law of Moses is not given as the meaning of the linen; 19:8 says it is the righteous acts of the saints.
The songs of heaven
Songs of heaven are sung in this chapter, but the linen is explained as the righteous acts of the saints (19:8).
The righteous acts of the saints
The blood of the martyrs
The blood of the martyrs is not what the linen is said to be; 19:8 says it is the righteous acts of the saints.
The prayers of the prophets
Prayers of the prophets are not what the linen represents; 19:8 explains it as the righteous acts of the saints.
In Revelation 19, who are called blessed?
The angel says, “Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb” (19:9).
Revelation 19:9
Those who flee to the wilderness
Fleeing to the wilderness is the woman’s story in Revelation 12:6; the blessing in 19:9 is for those invited to the marriage supper.
Those invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb
Those who sound the trumpets
Sounding the trumpets is the work of angels in Revelation 8–11; the blessing in 19:9 is for those invited to the marriage supper.
Those who rebuild the temple
Rebuilding the temple is not mentioned in Revelation 19; the blessing is for those invited to the marriage supper.
Those who sit on thrones in Jerusalem
Those seated on thrones are described in Revelation 20:4; the blessing in 19:9 is for those invited to the marriage supper.
In Revelation 19, how does the angel describe the message about the marriage supper?
The angel adds, “These are the true words of God” (19:9).
Revelation 19:9
A hidden mystery
A mystery is how Revelation 17:5 labels Babylon’s name; the angel calls these words “the true words of God.”
A difficult parable
Parables are not mentioned here; the angel calls these words “the true words of God” (19:9).
The true words of God
A sign for the churches
The churches receive the letters of Revelation 2–3; about the supper message, the angel says “These are the true words of God.”
A sealed prophecy
The sealed scroll belongs to Revelation 5–6; here the angel calls the message “the true words of God” (19:9).
In Revelation 19, what does John do when the angel speaks to him?
John says, “I fell at his feet to worship him,” but the angel stops him (19:10).
Revelation 19:10
He covers his face and weeps in fear
John does fall down, but to worship the angel, and he is stopped; nothing says he covers his face and weeps.
He blows a trumpet before the throne
Angels sound the trumpets in Revelation 8–11; John does not blow one before the throne in this scene.
He falls at the angel’s feet to worship him
He writes a new song of praise
John is told to write a blessing (19:9), but he does not compose a song; he falls to worship the angel.
He asks the angel for the small scroll
John does ask an angel for the small scroll in Revelation 10:9, but that is another scene; here he falls to worship.
In Revelation 19, whom does the angel tell John to worship?
The angel says, “Worship God!” (19:10).
Revelation 19:10
The Lamb’s bride
The bride is not to be worshiped; the angel says, “Worship God!” (19:10).
The heavenly host
The heavenly host is not named as an object of worship; the angel says, “Worship God!” (19:10).
The angel himself
The angel refuses worship, saying he is a fellow servant (19:10), and points John to God.
God
The elders
The elders are worshipers themselves (19:4); the angel tells John, “Worship God!” (19:10).
In Revelation 19, what is the testimony of Jesus called?
“The testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy” (19:10).
Revelation 19:10
The key of David
The key of David is a title in Revelation 3:7, not what 19:10 says the testimony of Jesus is.
The spirit of prophecy
The song of Moses
The song of Moses is sung in Revelation 15:3; 19:10 calls the testimony of Jesus the spirit of prophecy.
The seal of God
The seal of God is placed on servants in Revelation 7:3; the testimony of Jesus is called the spirit of prophecy (19:10).
The wisdom of the saints
The wisdom of the saints is not what the angel names; he says the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy (19:10).
In Revelation 19, what does John see standing open?
“Then I saw heaven standing open” (19:11).
Revelation 19:11
The abyss
The Abyss is opened in Revelation 9:2; what John sees standing open in 19:11 is heaven.
The temple curtain
The temple veil is torn in the Gospels (Matthew 27:51); in 19:11 John sees heaven standing open.
Heaven
The eastern gate
The eastern gate is from Ezekiel’s vision of the temple; in 19:11 John sees heaven standing open.
The sea of glass
The sea of glass stands before the throne (Revelation 4:6); what stands open in 19:11 is heaven.
In Revelation 19, what color is the horse John sees when heaven opens?
“There before me was a white horse” (19:11).
Revelation 19:11
Red
A red horse appears when the second seal is opened (Revelation 6:4), not when heaven opens in 19:11.
Black
A black horse belongs to the third seal (Revelation 6:5); the horse in 19:11 is white.
Pale green
The pale green horse carries Death (Revelation 6:8); the rider in 19:11 sits on a white horse.
White
Scarlet
A scarlet beast carries the woman in Revelation 17:3, but the horse in 19:11 is white.
In Revelation 19, what is the rider on the white horse called?
“Its rider is called Faithful and True” (19:11).
Revelation 19:11
Lion of Judah
Lion of Judah is the title in Revelation 5:5, not the name given to the rider in 19:11.
Faithful and True
Bright Morning Star
Bright Morning Star is the title in Revelation 22:16; the rider in 19:11 is called Faithful and True.
Holy and Living
Holy and Living is not the rider’s name; 19:11 says he is called Faithful and True.
Shepherd of Israel
Shepherd of Israel is the title in Psalm 80:1; the rider in 19:11 is called Faithful and True.
In Revelation 19, with what does the rider judge and wage war?
“With righteousness He judges and wages war” (19:11).
Revelation 19:11
Mercy
He judges with righteousness, not mercy, in 19:11; mercy is not named as the standard of His judging and war.
Fire
Fire is not said to be what He judges and wages war with; 19:11 says with righteousness.
Wisdom
Wisdom is not the standard named; 19:11 says He judges and wages war with righteousness.
Righteousness
Silence
Silence is not mentioned; 19:11 says He judges and wages war with righteousness.
In Revelation 19, what are the rider’s eyes like?
“He has eyes like blazing fire” (19:12).
Revelation 19:12
Shining bronze
Shining bronze describes the Son of Man’s feet in Revelation 1:15; His eyes are like blazing fire (19:12).
A burning lampstand
A burning lampstand is not the comparison; His eyes are like blazing fire (19:12).
A blazing fire
The sun at noon
The sun at noon is not the comparison for His eyes; 19:12 says blazing fire.
Crystal seas
Crystal seas are not the comparison; 19:12 says His eyes are like blazing fire.
In Revelation 19, what is on the rider’s head?
The rider has “many royal crowns on His head” (19:12).
Revelation 19:12
One golden crown
One golden crown is worn by the One like the Son of Man in Revelation 14:14; the rider in 19:12 has many royal crowns.
Twelve stars
Twelve stars crown the woman of Revelation 12:1; the rider in 19:12 has many royal crowns.
Many royal crowns
A linen turban
A linen turban is not mentioned; the rider wears many royal crowns (19:12).
Ashes and dust
Ashes and dust are signs of mourning, not what is on the rider’s head; he has many royal crowns (19:12).
In Revelation 19, who knows the rider’s written name?
He has “a name written on Him that only He Himself knows” (19:12).
Revelation 19:12
The angels only
The angels are not said to know it; the name is one “that only He Himself knows” (19:12).
The elders only
The elders are not said to know it; only He Himself knows the name (19:12).
John and the churches
John and the churches are not given the name; 19:12 says only He Himself knows it.
Only He Himself
The bride only
The bride is not said to know it; the name is one that only He Himself knows (19:12).
In Revelation 19, how is the rider’s robe described?
The rider “is dressed in a robe dipped in blood” (19:13).
Revelation 19:13
Torn and dusty
His robe is not torn and dusty; 19:13 says it is dipped in blood.
Dipped in blood
Woven with gold
His robe is not woven with gold; 19:13 says it is dipped in blood.
Scarlet and purple
Scarlet and purple clothe the great prostitute (Revelation 17:4), not the rider; his robe is dipped in blood (19:13).
Covered with stars
Stars crown the woman in Revelation 12:1, but the rider’s robe is dipped in blood (19:13).
In Revelation 19, what is the rider’s name called?
“His name is The Word of God” (19:13).
Revelation 19:13
Son of Man
Son of Man is how Jesus appears in Revelation 1:13, but the name given in 19:13 is The Word of God.
Alpha and Omega
Alpha and Omega is a title in Revelation 1:8; the name in 19:13 is The Word of God.
The Word of God
Emmanuel
Emmanuel means “God with us” (Matthew 1:23); the name given in 19:13 is The Word of God.
Root of Jesse
Root of Jesse is from Isaiah 11:10; the name given in 19:13 is The Word of God.
In Revelation 19, who follow the rider on the white horse?
“The armies of heaven, dressed in fine linen, white and pure, follow Him on white horses” (19:14).
Revelation 19:14
The kings of the earth
The kings of the earth gather against the rider (19:19); they do not follow him.
The armies of heaven
The seven churches
The seven churches are addressed in Revelation 2–3; the ones who follow the rider in 19:14 are the armies of heaven.
The souls under the altar
The souls under the altar are in Revelation 6:9; the followers in 19:14 are the armies of heaven.
The tribe of Judah only
The tribe of Judah is not named; the followers in 19:14 are the armies of heaven.
In Revelation 19, what are the armies of heaven riding?
The armies of heaven follow Him “on white horses” (19:14).
Revelation 19:14
Chariots of fire
Chariots of fire are from the story of Elijah (2 Kings 2:11); the armies in 19:14 ride white horses.
White horses
Winged creatures
Winged creatures surround the throne (Revelation 4:8), but the armies in 19:14 ride white horses.
Clouds
Clouds are not their mounts; 19:14 says they follow Him on white horses.
Golden carts
Golden carts are not mentioned; 19:14 says they follow Him on white horses.
In Revelation 19, what are the armies of heaven wearing?
The armies are “dressed in fine linen, white and pure” (19:14).
Revelation 19:14
Scarlet robes
Scarlet robes are not worn by the armies; 19:14 says fine linen, white and pure.
Armor of bronze
Armor of bronze is not mentioned; the armies are dressed in fine linen, white and pure (19:14).
Fine linen, white and pure
Sackcloth
Sackcloth is worn by the two witnesses (Revelation 11:3), not the armies of heaven in 19:14.
Purple garments
Purple garments clothe the great prostitute (Revelation 17:4); the armies wear fine linen, white and pure (19:14).
In Revelation 19, what proceeds from the rider’s mouth?
“From His mouth proceeds a sharp sword” (19:15).
Revelation 19:15
Fire and smoke
Fire and smoke come from the mouths of the horses in Revelation 9:17, not from the rider’s mouth in 19:15.
A sharp sword
A trumpet blast
A trumpet blast is not said to come from his mouth; 19:15 says a sharp sword does.
A river of life
A river of life flows from the throne in Revelation 22:1; from the rider’s mouth proceeds a sharp sword (19:15).
A chain
A chain is held by the angel in Revelation 20:1; from the rider’s mouth proceeds a sharp sword (19:15).
In Revelation 19, what does the rider strike down with the sharp sword from His mouth?
The sword is “to strike down the nations” (19:15).
Revelation 19:15
The stars
The stars are not struck down by the rider’s sword; it is for the nations (19:15).
The churches
The churches are not struck down by the sword; it is for the nations (19:15).
The nations
The mountains
Mountains are not the target of the sword in 19:15; it is to strike down the nations.
The angels
Angels are not the target; the sword in 19:15 is for striking down the nations.
In Revelation 19, with what will the rider rule the nations?
“He will rule them with an iron scepter” (19:15).
Revelation 19:15
A shepherd’s staff
A shepherd’s staff is not what he rules with in 19:15; the verse says an iron scepter (compare Psalm 2:9).
A golden scepter
A golden scepter is held out by the king in Esther 5:2, but 19:15 says an iron scepter.
An iron scepter
A silver trumpet
A silver trumpet is not his tool for ruling; he rules with an iron scepter (19:15).
A cedar rod
A cedar rod is not mentioned; he will rule the nations with an iron scepter (19:15).
In Revelation 19, what does the rider tread?
The rider “treads the winepress of the fury of the wrath of God the Almighty” (19:15).
Revelation 19:15
The sea of glass mixed with fire before the throne
The sea of glass mixed with fire is where the conquerors stand in Revelation 15:2; the rider does not tread it.
The winepress of the fury of the wrath of God the Almighty
The outer courts of the temple in Jerusalem
The temple courts are not what he treads in 19:15; the verse names the winepress of God’s wrath.
The valley full of dry bones in Ezekiel’s vision
The valley of dry bones is from Ezekiel 37:1–14, not what the rider treads in 19:15.
The great river Euphrates, dried up for the kings
The Euphrates is dried up in Revelation 16:12; the rider in 19:15 treads the winepress of God’s wrath.
In Revelation 19, what name is written on the rider’s robe and on His thigh?
“KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS” is written on His robe and on His thigh (19:16).
Revelation 19:16
Prince of Peace
Prince of Peace is a title in Isaiah 9:6, not the name written on his robe and thigh in 19:16.
Holy, Holy, Holy
Holy, Holy, Holy is the cry of the living creatures (Revelation 4:8), not the name on the rider’s robe.
King of kings and Lord of lords
Shepherd of the nations
Shepherd of the nations is not the name written; 19:16 says KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS.
Son of David
Son of David is a title in Matthew 1:1, not the name written on the rider’s robe in 19:16.
In Revelation 19, where does John see the angel who calls the birds?
“Then I saw an angel standing in the sun” (19:17).
Revelation 19:17
In the temple
The temple is where angels appear in other scenes (Revelation 15:6), but 19:17 puts this angel in the sun.
On a mountain
A mountain is not where this angel stands; 19:17 says in the sun.
In the sun
By the sea
A sea is where an angel stands in Revelation 10:2, but in 19:17 the angel stands in the sun.
At the altar
The altar is where another angel stands in Revelation 8:3; this angel stands in the sun (19:17).
In Revelation 19, whom does the angel in the sun call with a loud voice?
The angel “cried out in a loud voice to all the birds flying overhead” (19:17).
Revelation 19:17
All the saints
He does not call the saints; he calls the birds flying overhead (19:17).
All the nations
He does not call the nations; he calls the birds flying overhead (19:17).
All the birds flying overhead
The seven churches
The seven churches are addressed in Revelation 2–3; here he calls all the birds flying overhead (19:17).
The living creatures
The living creatures stand around the throne (Revelation 4:6); the angel in 19:17 calls the birds.
In Revelation 19, what is the birds’ gathering called?
The angel says, “Come, gather together for the great supper of God” (19:17).
Revelation 19:17
The feast of tabernacles
The feast of Tabernacles is an Old Testament festival; the birds are called to the great supper of God (19:17).
The great supper of God
The marriage supper of the Lamb
The marriage supper of the Lamb is for invited guests (19:9); the birds are called to a different gathering.
The bread of heaven
The bread of heaven recalls manna (Exodus 16:4); the birds are called to the great supper of God (19:17).
The table of shewbread
The table of the bread of the Presence is in the tabernacle (Exodus 25:30); the birds are called to the great supper of God.
In Revelation 19, which people are specifically named among those whose flesh the birds will eat?
The flesh to be eaten is that of “kings and commanders and mighty men” (19:18).
Revelation 19:18
Priests and Levites
Priests and Levites are not named in the list in 19:18.
Shepherds and tax collectors
Shepherds and tax collectors are not named in the list in 19:18.
Kings, commanders, and mighty men
Prophets and scribes
